segments.text: [point_screen] Seoul has started testing self-driving buses on two night routes. The city says the buses will help night workers get home when other transport has stopped. [A:nod] A safety driver stays on board during the trial.

segments.headline: Barcelona trials a fleet of delivery robots
segments.text: [point_screen] Twenty delivery robots have started carrying parcels through two districts of Barcelona. The trial will run for six months, Circuit Weekly reports. [B:nod] The robots travel at walking pace and stop for pedestrians.

segments.headline: Chipmaker unveils a laptop processor
segments.text: [point_screen] A chipmaker has unveiled a new laptop processor it says can run for 20 hours on a single charge. The first laptops using it will go on sale in the spring. [A:nod] Independent reviewers have not yet tested the claim, according to Circuit Weekly.

segments.headline: Swedish recycling plant recovers gold
segments.text: A recycling plant in Sweden says it can recover 1 kilogram of gold from 40,000 old phones. The company wants to process 2 million phones a year, Circuit Weekly reports. [B:look_partner]

segments.headline: Medicine-carrying drones expand across Rwanda
segments.text: And finally: drones now deliver medicine to 400 health centres across Rwanda, the operator says. The average flight takes about 30 minutes. [A:look_partner] Health workers order supplies by text message. Blood and vaccines make up most of the deliveries.
[nod] I have questions. Most of them start with how.
That's TECH BYTES. [nod] From Ada Volt and from me, thanks for watching. More news around the clock on GLOBIT 24.
[nod] This is NEWS IN 60. I'm Sam Night.

segments.headline: Norway raises interest rates
segments.text: [point_screen] Norway’s central bank has unexpectedly raised its main interest rate to 4.75 percent. Most economists had expected no change. Mortgage rates are expected to follow within weeks, according to Bitport Herald.

segments.headline: Rice prices ease in Asia
segments.text: [point_screen] Rice prices in Asia have fallen 8 percent since July after strong harvests in Thailand and Vietnam. Traders say supplies look healthy for the rest of the year.

segments.headline: Rover finds layered rocks on Mars
segments.text: [point_screen] A Mars rover has photographed layered rocks in what scientists believe was an ancient lake bed. The layers could hold clues about past water on the planet, Starfield Journal reports.

segments.headline: New glowing mushroom species found
segments.text: [point_screen] Biologists have described a new species of glowing mushroom found in the Atlantic forest of Brazil. It emits a soft green light at night, according to Starfield Journal.

segments.headline: Rocket launches probe to study Sun's poles
segments.text: [point_screen] A rocket has launched a probe that will study the Sun's poles for the first time. The journey to its final orbit will take 3 years, Starfield Journal reports.

segments.headline: Paris unveils plans to plant 170,000 trees
segments.text: [point_screen] The city of Paris has announced plans to plant 170,000 trees by 2030 to cool the city in summer.
That's the minute. Stay with us on GLOBIT 24. [papers]

segments.headline: Solar eclipse visible across northern Spain
segments.text: [point_screen] A total solar eclipse will be visible across northern Spain next August, Starfield Journal reports. Astronomers say the shadow will cross Bilbao and Valencia. [B:nod] Hotels along the path of the shadow report that many rooms are already booked.
[nod] Logged, Dr Reyes.
[look_partner] UNIT-8, our number of the day.

segments.headline: Scientists map ocean floor near Antarctica
segments.text: [count] Our number of the day: 50,000. A research ship has mapped 50,000 square kilometres of sea floor near Antarctica. The maps reveal underwater canyons and an extinct volcano, according to Starfield Journal. [A:nod]

segments.headline: Glacier in the Alps shrinks by 3 percent
segments.text: [point_screen] Measurements show a large glacier in the Alps lost 3 percent of its volume this summer, Starfield Journal reports. Scientists say the ice is now thinner than at any time since records began. [B:nod] A lake has formed at the foot of the ice where there was none twenty years ago.
[nod] The Alps. I have checked it twice.
Noted, UNIT-8. Thank you.

segments.headline: Ancient footprints found on a beach in Wales
segments.text: [point_screen] Storms have uncovered footprints left on a beach in Wales about 7,000 years ago. The team warns that the next storm could wash them away, according to Starfield Journal. [A:nod] Researchers say adults and children walked there together. The prints are preserved in a layer of hardened mud that is usually covered by sand.
[nod] Still to come: astronauts grow tomatoes on the space station.

segments.headline: Study: city trees cut summer temperatures
segments.text: [point_screen] A study of 90 European cities found that streets with many trees were about 2 degrees cooler in summer. Researchers say parks also reduced heat-related illness. [B:look_partner]

segments.headline: Giant tortoises return to a Galápagos island
segments.text: [point_screen] Rangers have released 50 young giant tortoises on an island in the Galápagos where the species vanished about 100 years ago. “It is a homecoming,” a park ranger said. [A:nod] The young tortoises were bred at a centre on another island. Rangers will track them with small radio tags, Starfield Journal reports.

quote.text: It is a homecoming

segments.headline: Comet will pass close enough to see
segments.text: [point_screen] A comet discovered last year will pass close to Earth this week and should be visible with binoculars just after sunset. Astronomers advise looking low in the western sky about half an hour after the sun goes down. [B:nod] It will not return for about 6,000 years, according to Starfield Journal.

segments.headline: Astronauts grow tomatoes on the space station
segments.text: And finally: astronauts on the International Space Station have harvested tomatoes grown in a small greenhouse. Scientists want to learn how to feed crews on long missions, Starfield Journal reports. [B:look_partner] The plants grew under red and blue lights in about three months.
I will keep one sensor pointed upwards, Dr Reyes. For the record.
That's COSMOS DESK. [nod] From UNIT-8 and from me, thank you for watching. Stay with us on GLOBIT 24.

[serious] Seville records 44 degrees as Spain issues heat alert. Canada and Mexico sign an agreement on clean water projects. Morocco desert solar plant reaches full power. Good morning, and welcome to WORLD NOW. [nod] I'm Paco Pixel, with Lola Byte. [B:nod]

segments.headline: Seville records 44 degrees
segments.text: [lean_in] In Seville, temperatures reached 44 degrees Celsius on Wednesday, the highest of the summer. Spain’s weather agency has issued a red alert for the south. Some schools have moved lessons to the early morning, according to Bitport Herald.

segments.headline: Canada, Mexico in clean water deal
segments.text: [raise_hand] Canada and Mexico have signed an agreement to fund clean water projects in rural communities. The two governments will share the cost of 50 new treatment plants, Pixelburg Post reports. [A:nod]

segments.headline: Morocco desert solar plant reaches full power
segments.text: [count] Our number of the day: more than 1 million. A large solar plant on the edge of the Sahara in Morocco is now running at full power. Its operator says it supplies electricity for more than 1 million people. [B:nod]

segments.headline: Cairo museum opens wing for ancient boats
segments.text: Thanks, Paco. A museum in Cairo has opened a new wing to show two ancient wooden boats. Curators say the larger boat is 43 metres long and was rebuilt from 1,200 pieces. [A:look_partner] Restorers spent eight years reassembling the larger vessel, according to Pixelburg Post.

segments.headline: Moderate earthquake shakes northern Chile
segments.text: [raise_hand] A magnitude 5.8 earthquake shook northern Chile on Tuesday morning, Pixelburg Post reports. Emergency services say there are no reports of damage or injuries. [B:nod] The quake was felt in the port city of Antofagasta.

segments.headline: Court orders Amsterdam airport to cut night flights
segments.text: [raise_hand] A court in the Netherlands has ordered Amsterdam’s main airport to cut night flights by a third from next year. The airport says it will appeal. [A:nod]

segments.headline: Rangers film a rare snow leopard and two cubs
segments.text: Rangers in Nepal have filmed a rare snow leopard with two cubs in the Himalayas, according to Bitport Herald. “It is a very hopeful sign for the species,” a park official said. [B:look_partner]

quote.text: It is a very hopeful sign for the species

segments.text: [nod] Still to come: Brazil reports a sharp fall in Amazon deforestation.

segments.headline: Brazil reports fall in Amazon deforestation
segments.text: [point_screen] Brazil's space agency says deforestation in the Amazon fell by 30 percent over the past twelve months. Satellite images show the lowest level of clearing in a decade. [A:look_partner] Officials credit more inspections and fines for illegal clearing. Environmental groups welcomed the figures but say clearing is still rising in some states.

segments.headline: Mexico City closes historic centre to cars
segments.text: [point_screen] Now, around the world in 30 seconds. Mexico City will close the streets of its historic centre to cars every Sunday from next month.

segments.headline: Ghana volunteers plant 1m mangrove trees
segments.text: Volunteers in Ghana have planted one million mangrove seedlings along the coast near Accra.

segments.headline: Wellington schools trial a four-day week
segments.text: Ten schools in Wellington, New Zealand, will trial a four-day week for one term.

segments.headline: Dublin hospitals under pressure
segments.text: Hospitals in Dublin say their emergency departments are under severe pressure after a rise in flu cases.

segments.headline: Venice raises its sea barriers in a test
segments.text: Venice has raised its sea barriers for a test ahead of the autumn high tides, Bitport Herald reports.

segments.headline: Seoul festival lights up the Han river
segments.text: And finally: a festival in Seoul lit up the sky over the Han river with a show of 1,000 drones. Organisers said about 200,000 people watched from the riverbanks. [A:nod] The drones formed the shape of a whale above the water.

segments.headline: Rail strike halts most trains across Germany
segments.text: [point_screen] In Germany, a 24-hour strike by rail workers has halted most long-distance trains. The operator says only one in five services is running, and unions say talks over pay have stalled. Many commuters switched to buses and car shares for the day, according to Ledger Line.

segments.headline: Airline orders 100 new fuel-efficient jets
segments.text: [point_screen] A European airline has ordered 100 new short-haul jets in a deal worth about 12 billion dollars. Deliveries will start in 2028, Ledger Line reports. The airline says the new aircraft burn about 20 percent less fuel than the planes they replace.

segments.headline: Bank of Canada holds interest rates
segments.text: [point_screen] The Bank of Canada has kept its main interest rate unchanged at 3.5 percent. Policymakers in Ottawa said inflation is easing but they want more evidence before cutting.

segments.headline: North Sea wind farm starts supplying power
segments.text: [point_screen] An offshore wind farm in the North Sea has started supplying electricity. The developer says its 140 turbines can power about 1.2 million homes. Power reaches the shore through cables laid along the seabed.

segments.headline: UK inflation rises unexpectedly
segments.text: [point_screen] Inflation in the United Kingdom rose to 3.8 percent in September, up from 3.4 percent in August, official figures show. Economists had expected it to stay flat, according to Ledger Line. Food and energy prices drove the rise.

segments.headline: Chocolate makers warn of higher prices
segments.text: [point_screen] Several chocolate makers say they will raise prices again because cocoa remains near record levels. Cocoa has more than doubled in price in two years, Ledger Line reports. Poor weather has hit harvests in West Africa, which grows most of the world's cocoa.

segments.headline: Electric car sales overtake diesel in Europe
segments.text: [count] Our number of the day: 17 percent. Sales of fully electric cars overtook diesel cars in Europe last month for the first time, an industry group says. Electric models made up 17 percent of new cars.
That's your MONEY MINUTE. I'm Penny Sterling. Stay with us on GLOBIT 24. [papers]

segments.headline: Tokyo stocks close at record high
segments.text: [point_screen] Tokyo's main stock index closed at a record high, driven by shares of chipmakers. The index has gained 21 percent since January, according to Ledger Line.

segments.headline: Scotland's first tidal power plant goes live
segments.text: [point_screen] A tidal power station off the north coast of Scotland has started sending electricity to the grid. The operator says its 4 turbines can power 7,000 homes.

segments.headline: Coffee futures reach ten-year high
segments.text: [point_screen] Around the world. First, Brazil. Coffee prices have climbed to their highest level in ten years after poor harvests in Brazil and Vietnam.

segments.headline: New York stocks close at record high
segments.text: Now to New York. Stock markets in New York closed at a record high on Thursday, Ledger Line reports.

segments.headline: Shipping costs fall
segments.text: [point_screen] The cost of shipping a container from Shanghai to Rotterdam has fallen by 20 percent in a month. Analysts say congestion at major ports is easing.

segments.headline: Oil prices slide
segments.text: [point_screen] Oil prices fell for a third day as traders expect weaker demand this winter. Brent crude dropped 2 percent to 71 dollars a barrel.
That's the minute. Stay with us on GLOBIT 24. [papers]

[serious] Heavy rain floods streets in coastal towns of Kerala. Hurricane Elena makes landfall on Mexico’s Yucatán coast. Wildfire near Marseille forces thousands to evacuate. Good morning, and welcome to WORLD NOW. [nod] I'm Paco Pixel, with Lola Byte. [B:nod]

segments.headline: Heavy rain floods streets in Kerala
segments.text: [lean_in] Heavy monsoon rain has flooded streets in several coastal towns in Kerala, India. Local authorities have opened 120 relief camps and closed schools for two days. Forecasters expect more heavy rain over the next three days, Pixelburg Post reports.

segments.headline: Hurricane Elena hits Mexico’s Yucatán coast
segments.text: [lean_in] Hurricane Elena has made landfall near Cancún with winds of 180 kilometres per hour, according to Pixelburg Post. Mexico’s civil protection agency says about 1.2 million homes are without power and 40,000 people have gone to shelters. “This is a life-threatening situation,” the agency said.

quote.text: This is a life-threatening situation

segments.headline: Marseille wildfire forces thousands to flee
segments.text: [lean_in] Firefighters are battling a wildfire on a pine ridge north of Marseille. About 3,000 residents have been moved from three villages, local officials say, and a motorway has been closed. Water-bombing planes are flying over the ridge, Bitport Herald reports.

segments.headline: Iceland volcano erupts again
segments.text: [point_screen] In Iceland, a fissure eruption has started again on the Reykjanes peninsula, according to Pixelburg Post. Scientists say lava is flowing away from nearby towns and flights are not affected. [A:nod] It is the latest in a series of eruptions in the area since 2021.

segments.headline: Bangkok airports handle record 6m passengers
segments.text: Thanks, Lola. [count] Our number of the day: 6 million. Bangkok's airports handled a record 6 million passengers last month, officials said. Hotels in the city report an occupancy rate of 85 percent. [B:look_partner]

segments.headline: Carmaker to close Turin plant
segments.text: [point_screen] A carmaker says it will close its plant near Turin by the end of next year. Unions say 2,400 jobs are at risk. [A:nod] [look_partner] Paco.

segments.headline: Coral recovers on parts of Great Barrier Reef
segments.text: [point_screen] Scientists say coral cover has grown on parts of the Great Barrier Reef for a second year. “The reef is showing it can bounce back when it gets a break,” a lead researcher said. [B:nod] Researchers warn that another hot summer could undo the gains, Bitport Herald reports.

quote.text: The reef is showing it can bounce back when it gets a break

segments.text: [nod] Still to come: Lisbon opens a new riverside tram line.

segments.headline: Japan's bullet trains mark a record year
segments.text: [point_screen] Rail operators in Japan say their bullet trains ran with an average delay of under one minute last year, a record. More than 160 million passengers used the network, according to Pixelburg Post. [A:look_partner] The fastest trains on the line reach 320 kilometres an hour. Operators credit new signalling and longer maintenance windows at night.

segments.headline: Storm forces ferry cancellations
segments.text: [point_screen] Now, around the world in 30 seconds. First, the Greek islands. Strong winds have forced ferry operators to cancel sailings between Athens and several Greek islands.

segments.headline: Kenya switches on its largest solar farm
segments.text: In Kenya, a solar farm north of Nairobi has started supplying power to the national grid, Pixelburg Post reports.

segments.headline: Peru archaeologists find 3,000-year-old temple
segments.text: Archaeologists in Peru say they have found the remains of a temple about 3,000 years old in the northern Andes.

segments.headline: Norway opens a 27 kilometre road tunnel
segments.text: Now to Western Norway. A 27 kilometre road tunnel under a fjord has opened on the west coast of Norway, Bitport Herald reports.

segments.headline: Panama Canal reopens after a day-long closure
segments.text: The Panama Canal has reopened to ships after fog closed it for a day, according to Ledger Line.

segments.headline: Lisbon opens a new riverside tram line
segments.text: And finally: Lisbon has opened a new tram line along the Tagus river. The city says the 9 kilometre route will carry 40,000 passengers a day. [A:nod] “This line will change how people move around the old town,” the mayor said. It is the first new tram route in the city for more than 20 years.

quote.text: This line will change how people move around the old town

segments.text: [nod] Quietly encouraging.
High praise, by your standards.
